MINUTES

  MAY 13, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Fire Department Assistant Chief Brian Kane.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2025 “WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS MONTH”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation to Los Angeles County Fire Department
Assistant Chief Kane, declaring May 2025 as Wildfire Preparedness Month.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2025 “MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS
  MONTH”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation declaring May 2025 as Mental Health
Awareness Month.

C.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2025 “MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation declaring May 2025 as Maternal Mental
Health Awareness Month.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ spoke personally about the importance of Maternal Mental
Health and resources available.

D.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2025 “OLDER AMERICANS MONTH”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation declaring May 2025 as Older Americans
Month. The proclamation was presented to members of Palos Verdes Peninsula Village who
were in attendance, including Laura Diepenbrock, Judy Bain and Kenneth and Harriet
Servis, as well as Peninsula Seniors member Tom Hyatt also in attendance.

E.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 17, 2025 “NATIONAL KIDS TO PARKS DAY”

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation declaring May 17, 2025 as National Kids to
Parks Day.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 13, 2025
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT REQUEST FOR RATE ADJUSTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Waste Management’s request for a
  rate adjustment on all levels of service as included in the attached FY 2025-26
  Collection Service Rate Schedule effective July 1, 2025 and approve the addition of
  7x/week commercial service rates and 3x/week manure collection rates.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked Waste Management for their collaborative partnership
with the City.

The increased labor costs were explained by Subcommittee Members COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHMITZ and MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, as well as Waste Management Senior
Account Executive Erick Quintero, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Discussion ensued about the high costs of recycling, high staff turnover and changes in the
workforce post-COVID.

Discussion also ensued about the modified route schedule with less missed collections and
less complaints.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE WASTE MANAGEMENT’S REQUEST FOR A RATE
  ADJUSTMENT ON ALL LEVELS OF SERVICE AS INCLUDED IN THE
  ATTACHED FY 2025-26 COLLECTION SERVICE RATE SCHEDULE
  EFFECTIVE JULY 1, 2025 AND APPROVE THE ADDITION OF 7X/WEEK
  COMMERCIAL SERVICE RATES AND 3X/WEEK MANURE COLLECTION
  RATES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO GEOSYNTEC CONSULTING INCORPORATED’S
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL
  ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR DRY WELL STORM DRAIN OPERATIONS &
  MAINTENANCE (O&M) PROJECT AT PVDE & BRIDLEWOOD CIRCLE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Third Amendment to the
  Professional Services Agreement (PSA) (attached) with Geosyntec Consultants, Inc.,
  to provide one year of Operations & Maintenance (O&M) services of the Dry Wells,
  located on PVDE and Bridlewood Circle, in a not-to-exceed amount of $27,000, all to
  the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba explained that the maintenance is not something the City’s
maintenance staff would be able to perform, however the City hopes to contract with the
subcontractor that installed the Dry Wells to perform maintenance in future years, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 13, 2025
 E.  ORDINANCE NO. 751 ADOPTING UPDATED FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY ZONES AS
  RECOMMENDED BY THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF FORESTRY AND FIRE
  PROTECTION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 51178

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss the issues related to adoption of the updated Fire Severity Zone
  maps; 4) Introduce for first reading, Ordinance No. 751; 5) Continue the Public
  Hearing for a second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 751, to the City Council
  Meeting of May 27, 2025.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Discussion ensued about the changes in the latest fire maps, possible changes in insurance
for residents, while also discussing the need to not be complacent or change any
precautionary measures the City and residents take to prevent fires.

Los Angeles County Fire Department Assistant Chief Kane explained that properties that
are no longer in the “Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones” will no longer get annual
inspections by the Fire Department starting in 2026. Chief Kane further explained that Cal
Fire developed these maps independently, using advanced fire modeling including artificial
intelligence, weather patterns, historical fire data, wind directions, aspects of slopes and
canyons etc.

Discussion ensued about the distinction between building code requirements and the Los
Angeles County Fire Department’s requirements related to the map changes.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that unless there is policy direction otherwise by the
Council, staff’s intent is to continue wildfire prevention and preparedness City initiatives,
education and outreach.

Community Development Director Naughton explained that portions of the City are located
in the “Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone” therefore all construction and properties within
the City are subject to the requirements under the “Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone.”
That triggers a process for any accessory structures or additions to single family homes to
go through a separate review process with a fuel modification where they look at landscaping
plans defensible space.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 751 AND CONTINUE
  THE PUBLIC HEARING FOR A SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF
  ORDINANCE NO. 751, TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF MAY 27, 2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 751 by title.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

MAY 13, 2025
